summary: The note describes the remainder of the Communist Party of Lithuania, which operated in 1990-91 on the platform of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union under Mykolas Burokevičius after the 'traditional' party declared independence from its Soviet counterpart. It played a major role in the January 1991 Events in Lithuania and in initiating the National Salvation Committee. The party was banned in August 1991 and, although still illegal, is affiliated with the Union of Communist Parties — Communist Party of the Soviet Union (UCP-CPSU) led by Gennady Zyuganov.
one_line: Account of the Lithuanian Communist Party's remnant faction in 1990-91, its role in the January 1991 events, its August 1991 ban, and later affiliation with the UCP-CPSU.
key_facts: The remainder of the Communist Party of Lithuania existed in 1990-91 on the platform of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.
The remainder was led by Mykolas Burokevičius in 1990-91.
The 'traditional' Communist Party of Lithuania declared independence from its Soviet Union counterpart.
The Communist Party of Lithuania played a major role in the January 1991 Events in Lithuania.
The Communist Party of Lithuania initiated the creation of the National Salvation Committee.
The Communist Party of Lithuania was banned in August 1991.
As of the note, the Communist Party of Lithuania is still illegal.
The Communist Party of Lithuania is affiliated to the Union of Communist Parties — Communist Party of the Soviet Union (UCP-CPSU).
The UCP-CPSU is headed by Gennady Zyuganov.
